MUKKA PROTEINS EXPANDS BENGALURU WET-WASTE BIOCONVERSION INTO INSECT PROTEIN & BIO-PRODUCTS 🚀

🏭 Mukka Proteins has detailed commercial-scale expansion of its Black Soldier Fly (BSF) bioconversion operations in Bengaluru, converting municipal wet waste into high-value bio-products.

📈 Processing infrastructure is designed for up to 1,000 tonnes per day (TPD) of organic wet waste; current intake is around 200 TPD.

🎯 Capacity utilisation is targeted to rise to around 400 TPD by March 2027, followed by gradual scaling towards 1,000 TPD by December 2027.

♻️ BSF larval processing can deliver around 80% mass reduction of raw organic waste within 10–14 days.

🐛 Output products include insect protein meal, feed-grade insect oil, organic frass compost and humic acid/bio-stimulants.

🥩 Insect protein meal contains 50%+ crude protein and can substitute fishmeal and soybean meal in aquafeed, poultry and premium pet food.

🌍 Global insect meal & lipids market is projected to exceed $3.5 billion by 2030, while the agricultural bio-stimulant market is indicated to be growing at 11%+ CAGR.

🌱 The initiative also supports municipal waste diversion, lower methane emissions and potential carbon-credit opportunities.

🟢 Impact: Positive — scaling waste-to-value capacity toward 1,000 TPD opens new revenue streams in insect protein, oils, compost and bio-stimulants while strengthening Mukka Proteins’ circular bio-economy positioning.

MONEYBOXX FINANCE LAUNCHES ‘SMARTBIZ LOAN’ DIGITAL LENDING PRODUCT 🚀

📱 Moneyboxx Finance has launched its Digital Lending Platform in partnership with Trusave Fintech Private Limited (“Bachat”).

💼 The new product, SmartBiz Loan, is an unsecured digital lending product targeted at underserved small businesses.

🤝 Bachat will act as a Lending Service Provider (LSP) and support customer acquisition, digital onboarding, operations and servicing.

🏦 Moneyboxx will remain the lender and will independently evaluate and underwrite all loan applications as per its credit policies.

⚙️ The partnership combines Bachat’s technology and digital distribution capabilities with Moneyboxx’s credit underwriting, lending and servicing expertise.

📈 The digital platform will complement Moneyboxx’s existing branch-led lending model, helping expand its addressable customer base and build a more scalable, diversified lending franchise.

📅 Launch Date: August 31, 2026.

🟢 Impact: Positive — digital distribution can expand customer reach, improve scalability and potentially generate operating leverage as Moneyboxx’s digital loan portfolio grows.

HUHTAMAKI INDIA TO CLOSE BADDI PRESSURE-SENSITIVE LABELS UNIT; CONSOLIDATE OPERATIONS

📌 Huhtamaki India has approved closure of its Pressure Sensitive (PS) Labels manufacturing operations at Baddi, Himachal Pradesh.

🔄 The company will consolidate its PS Labels operations at its Ambernath and Bangalore facilities.

⚙️ Move is aimed at improving operational efficiency, capacity utilisation, economies of scale and cost rationalisation.

💰 Baddi PS Labels unit contributed ₹21.88 Cr turnover in FY2025, accounting for only 0.92% of company revenue.

📅 Closure is expected to be effective from October 10, 2026.

📊 Company said the closure is not material from a materiality-threshold perspective.

🟢 Impact: Mildly Positive — consolidation of a small unit should improve manufacturing efficiency and cost structure, with limited impact on overall revenue.

HAPPIEST MINDS | MERGER WITH ITC INFOTECH

Merger Update
- Happiest Minds to merge with ITC Infotech.
- Combined entity targets annualised revenue of ~₹7,033 Cr (~US$1 Bn) by FY28.
- Combined workforce of 19,000+ professionals.
- Will serve 800+ customers across 30+ countries.

Strategic Synergy
- Combines AI, digital engineering, cloud, data and cybersecurity capabilities.
- Adds strengths in enterprise transformation, SAP, PLM and Industry 4.0.
- Focus on building an AI-first technology services platform.
- Aims to compete for larger global transformation programs.
- Expansion focus across North America and Europe.
- Sector diversification across CPG, Hospitality, Manufacturing, EdTech, BFSI and Healthcare.

Deal Structure
- ITC Infotech to acquire ~22.1% stake in Happiest Minds for ₹1,330 Cr.
- Merger to be executed through a share swap.
- Happiest Minds shareholders to receive 25 ITC Infotech shares for every 81 shares held.
- ITC Ltd to become promoter of the merged entity with ~73.4% stake.

Key Takeaway
- Merger creates a ~US$1 Bn technology services platform.
- Stronger AI and enterprise capabilities could support larger global deals.
- ITC's ~73.4% promoter stake provides strategic backing.

RELIANCE, MRPL, CHENNAI PETRO: GLOBAL DIESEL REFINING MARGINS SET TO SURGE — GOLDMAN SACHS

📈 Goldman Sachs expects U.S. diesel refining margins to reach ~$63/barrel in 2027, sharply higher than its earlier forecast of $27/barrel.

🌍 European diesel refining margins are seen averaging around $49/barrel, compared with the earlier estimate of $19/barrel.

🔥 Global refining capacity remains tight due to refinery disruptions in the Middle East and Russia, while diesel inventories remain constrained.

🏭 Goldman estimates refinery outages are currently around 60% above seasonal averages, with diesel-market tightness expected to persist into next year.

⛽ Fuel exports from the Persian Gulf are running at only around 40% of pre-war levels, versus an estimated 70–80% for crude exports.

🇷🇺 Russia has also extended restrictions on diesel exports amid production constraints.

💰 Higher global diesel cracks/refining margins are supportive for refiners with meaningful export and diesel exposure, including Reliance Industries, MRPL and Chennai Petroleum.

🟢 Impact: Positive for Reliance, MRPL & Chennai Petro — sustained elevated diesel cracks could significantly improve GRMs and refining profitability.

📊 Authorities said the final amount of counterfeit currency is still being verified and the investigation remains ongoing.

🔴 Impact: Negative — the alleged ₹7.4 Cr counterfeit-note substitution raises serious internal-control and operational-risk concerns for PNB, though the matter is still under investigation.

FORTIS HEALTHCARE: DELHI HIGH COURT ORDERS FORENSIC AUDIT INTO HISTORICAL PROMOTER SHAREHOLDING MATTER

📌 Delhi High Court has directed the appointment of a forensic auditor in proceedings involving Daiichi Sankyo and Fortis’ erstwhile promoters, the Singh Brothers.

🔍 The forensic audit will primarily examine the disposition of the Singh Brothers’ shareholding in Fortis, subsequent change in control and the role of relevant stakeholders.

🏦 Inquiry will also cover the role of banks, financial institutions, erstwhile promoters and the then management of Fortis in relation to the transactions.

✅ Fortis clarified that no liability, penalty or fine has been imposed on the company under the order.

⚖️ The company was neither a party to the original dispute nor a judgment debtor in the execution proceedings.

📑 Fortis said the forensic audit is investigative in nature and does not by itself determine or fasten any liability on the company.

👨‍⚖️ Company is reviewing the judgment with legal counsel and will evaluate appropriate further action.

🟡 Impact: Neutral to Slightly Negative — no current financial liability has been imposed, but the forensic audit creates a near-term legal and regulatory overhang.

SUDARSHAN CHEMICAL DIVESTS VP4 FRANKFURT TO CELANESE; SHARPENS FOCUS ON CORE PIGMENTS BUSINESS

🤝 Sudarshan Chemical has agreed to sell its step-down subsidiary VP4 Frankfurt GmbH to Celanese Corporation, USA.

🏭 VP4 Frankfurt manufactures certain intermediates such as Diketene and primarily operates on a tolling basis for Nutrinova, an affiliate of Celanese and Mitsui & Co.

🔄 VP4 Frankfurt became part of Sudarshan following its acquisition of the Heubach Group.

📊 Nutrinova is VP4 Frankfurt’s principal customer, while only a small portion of output is consumed captively by Sudarshan.

🎯 Management said the divestment will allow Sudarshan to sharpen its strategic and operational focus on pigments and colorants, where it sees greater value creation potential.

🤝 Following completion, Nutrinova will continue supplying Sudarshan with the materials it requires, helping ensure continuity of supply.

💬 Management said the transaction places VP4 Frankfurt with the customer it already principally serves, while allowing Sudarshan to concentrate resources on its core businesses.

🟢 Impact: Positive — divestment of a non-core asset acquired through Heubach should simplify operations and improve management focus on higher-priority pigments and colorants businesses.

SUN PHARMA ; CO SIGNS U.S. MEDICINE PRICING & ACCESS AGREEMENT AT WHITE HOUSE

🤝 Sun Pharma participated in a White House signing ceremony alongside several global pharmaceutical companies to announce agreements with the U.S. government aimed at improving access to affordable medicines.

💊 Under the agreement, Sun Pharma will extend Most Favored Nation (MFN) pricing to state Medicaid programs.

📉 The company has also committed to MFN pricing for future innovative medicine launches in the U.S.

🛡️ In recognition of Sun Pharma’s U.S. investments, the agreement provides for a delay in Section 232 tariffs on innovative pharmaceutical products for more than two years.

🇺🇸 The U.S. is Sun Pharma’s largest market for innovative medicines and contributes approximately 27% of its global revenue.

🏭 Management reiterated that the U.S. remains a key investment market across clinical development, sales & marketing, APIs and finished-product manufacturing.

💰 Sun Pharma also highlighted its proposed $11.75 billion enterprise-value acquisition of Organon, underscoring its long-term commitment to the U.S. market.

🟡 Impact: Mixed to Positive — MFN pricing could pressure realizations on innovative drugs, but the multi-year tariff relief and improved policy visibility reduce a major U.S. regulatory risk for Sun Pharma.

Apollo Pipes is entering a new business—and raising ₹189 Cr to fund the next phase of growth.

Apollo Pipes has approved an investment plan of up to ₹300 Cr to establish subsidiary(ies) for entering the tiles & ceramics business.

Alongside this, Apollo Pipes plans to raise up to ₹189.1 Cr through preferential issuance of 31 lakh fully convertible warrants at ₹610 each.

Who is investing?

The proposed investors are:
AGDG Enterprises LLP — 12 lakh warrants
Rachita Gupta — 8 lakh
Gaurav Arora — 3 lakh
Rohit D Gupta — 2 lakh
Anshvardhan Modi — 2 lakh
Poonam Krishna Patel — 2 lakh
Ekta Tayal — 1 lakh
Sukumar Srinivas — 1 lakh

All are classified as non-promoter investors.

At full conversion, these 31 lakh warrants would represent approximately 6.31% of the post-issue diluted equity.

Why is this interesting?
The bigger story isn't simply the fundraise.

Apollo Pipes is looking to move beyond its traditional pipes & fittings business into tiles and ceramics, and the ₹300 Cr investment plan gives management significant capital flexibility to pursue this.

The reference to acquiring already operational and profitable manufacturing businesses is particularly worth watching. An acquisition-led entry could allow Apollo Pipes to enter the segment faster than building capacity entirely from scratch.

But this also changes the company's capital-allocation profile.

The key questions going forward are:
 - What business will Apollo acquire?
 - At what valuation?
 - How much of the ₹300 Cr will actually be deployed?
 - What margins/ROCE can the new business generate?
 - And can management create synergies with its existing distribution network?
 - The ₹189 Cr preferential issue provides the funding capacity.
 - The real test will be what Apollo Pipes does with that capital.

KSH INTERNATIONAL | COPPER IS THE PASS-THROUGH, EBITDA/TONNE IS THE STORY

Business Model
- Manufactures copper winding wires for transformers and motors.
- Reports business in two buckets.
- Specialized winding wires.
- Standard winding wires.
- No separate EV or T&D reporting segment.
- Copper largely passes through the P&L.

How To Read The Business
- Copper is procured after customer orders are received.
- Pricing is linked to prevailing LME copper prices.
- Higher copper prices inflate reported revenue.
- Revenue growth alone can therefore be misleading.
- EBITDA/tonne is the key operating metric.
- Core framework: Tonnes × EBITDA/tonne.

EBITDA/ Tonne | Key Metric
- Q1 FY26: ~₹66,000/tonne.
- Q4 FY26: ~₹74,000/tonne.
- Q1 FY27: ~₹93,000/tonne.
- FY27 comfort level: ~₹75,000/tonne.
- Q1 performance significantly exceeded the full-year comfort level.
- Sustainability of this level is the key monitorable.

Specialized Wires | Higher Value
- Specialized wires generate higher profitability than standard wires.
- CTC is the highest-value product within specialized wires.
- Q1 FY27 recorded a record CTC mix.
- Phase 1 capacity was front-loaded towards CTC.
- Phase 2 adds standard and EV capacity.
- Product mix expected to normalize over 2–3 quarters.

CTC | Core Strength
- CTC stands for continuously transposed conductor.
- Uses multiple thin enamelled copper strands.
- Strands are transposed to distribute current evenly.
- Conductors are additionally paper-wrapped.
- Primarily used in large power transformers.
- KSH holds a leading position in India's CTC market.

End-Market Mix
- ~75% of current business linked to large power transformers.
- Export contribution: ~27%.
- Exports were ~29% previously.
- Management targets exports at ~40%.
- Global transformer demand provides structural visibility.

Transformer Opportunity
- Global transformer OEMs reportedly hold 3–5 year order books.
- These are customer order books, not KSH's own order book.
- Five-year framework agreement signed with Hitachi Energy Global.
- Agreement does not specify quantity or pricing.
- Transformer demand provides long-term industry visibility.

Standard Wires | India Opportunity
- BIS is shifting imported standard wire demand towards Indian suppliers.
- Local sourcing can create additional domestic opportunity.
- Phase 2 capacity adds standard-wire capability.
- Mix shift can broaden the addressable market.

EV Opportunity
- 2W and 3W EV demand currently remains stronger.
- Passenger vehicles and buses are longer-dated opportunities.
- Meaningful passenger-car/bus opportunity expected around FY28–29.
- Phase 2 includes dedicated EV capacity.

Capacity Expansion
- Phase 1 was weighted towards CTC.
- Phase 2 expands standard and EV capabilities.
- New capacity increases addressable end markets.
- Product-specific capacity creates strategic flexibility constraints.
- Mix is expected to normalise as Phase 2 ramps up.

Capacity Allocation Risk
- Copper drawing capacity is relatively fungible.
- Insulation capacity is product-specific.
- CTC lines cannot manufacture EV wire.
- Each insulation line effectively commits capacity to an end market.
- Capacity decisions are made well ahead of demand.
- Typical lead time for such capacity decisions is ~18 months.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Reported revenue is heavily influenced by copper prices.
- Revenue growth and EBITDA margin should not be viewed in isolation.
- The key framework is tonnes × EBITDA/tonne.
- Q1 FY27 EBITDA/tonne of ~₹93,000 materially exceeded the ₹75,000 FY27 comfort level.
- CTC currently drives superior economics.
- Transformer exposure remains the dominant business.
- Standard and EV capacity will change the product mix over the next 2–3 quarters.
- Export expansion towards 40% provides another growth lever.
- The key question is whether elevated EBITDA/tonne can remain sustainable.

Earlier, a stock’s closing price was based on its VWAP during the final 30 minutes.

A fund could trade during this period, but it could not know in advance what the final closing price would be.

With CAS, closing orders are collected and matched at a single equilibrium price, helping index funds and ETFs trade closer to the same price used by their benchmark.

For F&O traders, this creates another interesting effect.

Large MSCI buy and sell orders will now enter the cash-market auction, while futures and options continue trading until 3:40 PM.

So large moves in affected stocks during CAS could also be reflected in Nifty and stock futures and options.

The important thing to remember is that nothing has necessarily changed in the companies themselves.

But if MSCI changes a stock’s place or weight in its indices, funds tracking those indices still have to buy or sell it.

So some stocks could see large flows during today’s CAS, purely because of an index change.

This is the first MSCI rebalance since the Closing Auction Session (CAS) was introduced in Indian markets.

And this is exactly the kind of situation CAS was designed for: allowing large closing orders from index funds and ETFs to be matched at the market’s actual closing price.

In the last rebalance, ETFs and index funds tracking MSCI had to adjust their holdings.

The additions were estimated to trigger around $1.38 billion of buying, while the deletions were estimated to lead to around $715 million of selling.

Overall, the rebalance was estimated to result in around ₹8,000–8,500 crore of net outflows from Indian stocks.

Just like the Nifty 50 tracks 50 large Indian stocks and the Sensex tracks 30, MSCI also creates stock indices.

Its MSCI India Index tracks around 165 large and mid-sized Indian companies.

ETFs and other index funds then track these indices, just like Nifty ETFs track the Nifty 50.

So when MSCI adds or removes a stock, or changes its weight in the index, these funds have to adjust their holdings too.

That can lead to large buying or selling in the affected stocks.

MSCI Index rebalancing is back today.

During the last two rounds, the Nifty fell around 0.5% to 1% near the close. Today, those heavy closing flows will meet the new Closing Auction Session (CAS) for the first time.

CAS was built for moments like this: handling large ETF and index-fund orders at the close.

FPIs Want Direct Exchange Access - A Headwind for Brokers, Not the Capital-Market Theme

Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) are pushing SEBI for direct access to stock exchanges, seeking to bypass broker infrastructure and connect their trading servers more directly with the exchanges for faster execution. If permitted, this could mark a meaningful change in the way institutional trades are routed in India. 

For brokers, the development is clearly a potential structural headwind, particularly for businesses that rely heavily on institutional execution and transaction-linked revenues. Direct connectivity could reduce the intermediary’s role in the execution chain and increase competitive pressure on brokerage economics. 

Importantly, however, this is an FPI request being considered by SEBI - not a SEBI proposal that has already been approved or implemented.

The impact also shouldn't be extrapolated to the entire capital-market ecosystem. Exchanges could actually benefit if faster and more efficient access encourages greater FPI participation, liquidity and trading volumes, while depositories such as CDSL and market-infrastructure businesses such as KFin and CAMS are largely insulated because their core functions remain essential irrespective of how an order reaches the exchange.

In other words, this could be negative for the intermediary but potentially positive for the underlying market infrastructure. 

For investors tracking the capital-market theme, the development looks more like a potential shift in value within the ecosystem rather than a threat to the broader structural story of rising market participation, institutionalisation and financialisation of Indian savings.

Many Problem: Solar led grid instability / Energy import / Pollution One solution: EV India is winning solar race. Solar supply a huge chunk of daytime power, pushing net grid demand sharply lower arnd noon. But demand peaks after sunset. That's the classic "duck curve" problem

~80 GW swing created largely by renewable output. The irony: clean power is available when demand isn't. Several states doing solar curtailment as the grid couldn't absorb all midday generation. So, next phase of green transition is tougher than just adding more solar panels

India imports ~90% of its crude oil needs & roughly half of its natural gas . Energy security remains one of the biggest economic vulnerabilities. Crude oil is among India's largest import items. Every $ oil prices widens the import bill = trade deficit = pressure on Rupee

Air pollution remains a public health emergency in major metros. Delhi frequently records PM2.5 levels many multiples above WHO norms, while Mumbai too has seen worsening air quality episodes. Solar, oil imports & air pollution are not separate challenges. They are connected

The common link is urban transport. A large share of oil consumption in metros comes from ICE cars commuting daily between home & office. Think about office parking lots. Vehicles remain parked for 8-10 hrs during the exact period when solar generation is highest

What if every major office complex became a daytime EV charging hub? Cars would consume power when solar generation is abundant, helping flatten the duck curve instead of deepening it.

Corp can accelerate this shift. EV subsidy for employees & workplace chargin infra can become part of CSR spend (2% of PBT) Vehicles in metros spend most working hours parked at offices. Converting 20%+ of parking capacity into chargers can create a daytime demand for solar power

One solution. Multiple benefits. More EVs = lower oil imports, cleaner city air, higher daytime power consumption, better solar utilisation & stable grid. Sometimes the smartest energy storage isn't a battery plant. It's millions of parked EVs connected to chargers.

CDMO | MULTI-DECADAL OPPORTUNITY

Industry Opportunity
- Global CDMO market: ~$170Bn.
- India remains a relatively small share of the global market.
- Innovators increasingly seek a second manufacturing geography.
- Switching an approved/filed manufacturer is difficult.
- New modalities such as peptides, ADCs and GLP-1 need specialised capacity.
- Creates a long-duration structural opportunity for Indian CDMOs.

Acutaas Chemicals | Highest Torque
- Pharma intermediates/CDMO remains the core earnings driver.
- First major programme backed by a 10-year supply contract.
- Four additional validated products in the pipeline.
- Potential peak revenue: ₹50–100 Cr per product.
- Management targets ~₹1,000 Cr CDMO revenue by FY28.
- FY27 revenue growth expected around 25%.
- Margins expected near FY26 levels.
- Battery electrolyte additives provide a second growth engine.
- Semiconductor chemicals through Korea JV provide FY28 optionality.
- One successful commercial molecule could materially reshape earnings.

Sai Life Sciences | Integrated Compounder
- Integrated discovery, development and commercial manufacturing platform.
- Works with large global pharmaceutical companies.
- Management sees 15–20% revenue CAGR over 3–5 years.
- Street expectations point to ~20%+ FY27 growth.
- 90%+ of targeted business reportedly already secured.
- Expected H1/H2 revenue mix: 40:60.
- EBITDA margin band: 28–30%.
- FY27 capex planned at ₹1,100–1,300 Cr.
- Capacity expected to increase from 700 KL to 1,150 KL.
- Peptides and ADCs add the next capability layer.

Aarti Pharmalabs | CDMO as the Kicker
- Business has three major engines: Xanthine, API and CDMO.
- Xanthine remains the established earnings base.
- CDMO is the key business capable of changing the mix.
- FY26 CDMO growth: 32%.
- FY27 CDMO growth guidance: 40–50%.
- Company targets 15–18% revenue and EBITDA CAGR.
- Long-term ambition: ~₹1,000 Cr each from Xanthine, API and CDMO.
- 50+ active CDMO projects.
- Majority of revenue comes from Phase-3/commercial programmes.
- Atali Block 1 is ramping up.
- Atali Block 2: ~₹149 Cr dedicated high-volume facility.
- Xanthine capacity planned from 6,000 to ~9,000–9,600 tonnes.

Shilpa Medicare | Platform Optionality
- Not yet a pure-play CDMO story.
- Formulations and API continue to fund the business.
- CDMO, peptides and biologics provide future optionality.
- Europe formulations offer near-term revenue opportunity.
- Rotigotine patch and NorUDCA are near-term opportunities.
- Oncology APIs and licensing provide additional potential.
- 25+ CDMO programmes in the pipeline.
- Three late-stage NCEs targeted for FY28.
- Exclusive OLC block provides FY27 optionality.
- Peptide/GLP-1 block expected to commission by end-FY27.
- Biologics CDMO and biosimilars build on ~₹150 Cr FY26 base.
- Growth depends heavily on utilisation of the expanded asset base.

OTHER QUALITY CDMO COMPOUNDERS
- Divi's Laboratories.
- Laurus Labs.
- Neuland Laboratories.
- Navin Fluorine.

FOUR DIFFERENT CDMO GAMES
- Acutaas: J-curve / highest earnings torque.
- Sai Life: Integrated discovery-to-commercial compounder.
- Aarti Pharmalabs: Established cash engine funding CDMO expansion.
- Shilpa Medicare: Platform optionality across CDMO, peptides and biologics.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- CDMO opportunity is driven by global supply-chain diversification.
- Approved-manufacturer switching costs create customer stickiness.
- New modalities are expanding the addressable opportunity.
- The key differentiator will be execution, customer quality and utilisation.
- Acutaas offers the highest potential earnings torque.
- Sai Life offers a more diversified compounding model.
- Aarti combines an established business with accelerating CDMO growth.
- Shilpa offers broader platform optionality as new capacity ramps.

Underappreciated SBI MF's distribution moat 

SBI MF's biggest advantage isn't fund performance. It's distribution. In India, bank-backed AMCs blessed with an edge as the bank branch is still the most powerful financial distribution channel
Investors trust banks with savings, salaries & FDs. Convincing a depositor to buy a bank-sponsored MF is far easier than acquiring a customer from scratch. Trust compounds over time
This trust factor is visible across the industry. 4 of India's top 5 AMCs are bank-backed. Even with rising competition, large AMCs have largely retained market share
SBI has the widest reach across the country, with one of the largest branch networks, customer bases & geographic presence among all financial institutions. That reach is difficult to replicate
Unlike most AMCs, SBI MF gets disproportionate support from its parent. SBI Bank contributes 35% of SBI MF's equity AUM. Compare that with just 8% for ICICI AMC & 6% for HDFC AMC
More interestingly, 40% of SBI MF's equity AUM comes through bank channels, versus 19% for ICICI AMC & 12% for HDFC AMC. SBI's distribution engine remains a major growth driver
Most banks operate open architecture & recommend products across AMCs based on suitability. SBI may have open architecture formally, but data suggests SBI customers get mostly SBI-branded investment products
The numbers are striking. 100% of SBI MF's promoter-bank sourced AUM sits with SBI, vs 70% for ICICI AMC & just 28% for HDFC AMC. That's about as captive as distribution gets
SBI's MF penetration opportunity is still huge. Average MF AUM per SBI branch is only ~10% of retail deposits per branch, implying a long runway for existing customers to migrate from deposits into MFs
The next leg of growth likely comes from B30 markets. SBI MF already has the highest B30 equity AUM share at 16%, ahead of ICICI AMC (12%) & HDFC AMC (11%)
SBI's deep Tier-2/Tier-3 presence matters. 66% of SBI MF's SIPs originate from B30 markets, giving it access to underpenetrated investors who are just beginning their financialization journey
The final edge is economics. SBI MF's distribution cost through SBI is just 65 bps, lower than HDFC AMC's 68 bps & ICICI AMC's 69 bps. Better reach + higher trust + lower cost = a distribution moat that's hard to disrupt

The Relationship Trump Misunderstood:
For three decades, China and emerging markets effectively exported disinflation to the developed world. They produced goods at a fraction of Western costs and shipped them to consumers in the US and Europe. The result: lower prices and higher purchasing power
The West got cheaper TVs, phones, clothes, furniture and industrial goods. China got manufacturing jobs, export growth and rising incomes. It wasn't a one-way relationship. Both sides benefited
As exports surged, China accumulated enormous foreign exchange reserves. Every dollar earned from exports added to a growing pool of savings that had to be invested somewhere
Those reserves served two purposes: protect the yuan from volatility and build strategic national wealth. China used them to buy foreign assets, resources, companies and financial securities around the world
A large portion of those reserves found their way into US Treasuries. China became one of the largest lenders to the US government, recycling export earnings back into America's financial system
This mattered because sustained Treasury demand helped keep long-term US interest rates lower than they otherwise would have been. Cheap imports lowered inflation. Treasury purchases lowered financing costs
In effect, China was helping on two fronts: suppressing goods inflation through low-cost manufacturing and supporting bond markets through reserve recycling. 
Trump focused heavily on one side of the equation: the trade deficit. From that perspective, China was exporting too much and manufacturing jobs were leaving America. This became the basis for tariffs and trade confrontation.
But the other side received less attention. Those same imports were keeping prices low for US consumers. Many products became affordable precisely because they were manufactured in lower-cost economies
The relationship also extended to capital markets. China's reserve accumulation created a steady source of demand for US government bonds, helping support the broader financial system
Today that world is changing. China is no longer a low-income economy desperate for export growth. Wages have risen, technology has improved and its economic influence is far greater than it was 20 years ago
The old model of unlimited cheap labour, ever-rising globalization and automatic reserve recycling is fading. Both countries increasingly view the relationship through a strategic lens rather than purely an economic one
As supply chains fragment and tariffs rise, the US may face more inflation from its own policy choices. Producing goods domestically or through alternative supply chains is often more resilient, but rarely cheaper
At the same time, if foreign demand for Treasuries becomes less predictable, bond investors may demand higher yields to absorb increasing government debt. Higher yields mean higher financing costs across the economy
The next decade may look very different from the last three. Less globalization, more strategic competition, potentially higher inflation and structurally higher interest rates. Markets are still figuring out what that world looks like
Bottom line: The US-China relationship wasn't simply buyer vs seller. It was a system where goods, capital and inflation dynamics were deeply intertwined. Breaking that system may create consequences on both sides.

**AUTO ANCILLARIES | NEXT LEG OF GROWTH**

**Sona BLW**
- EPS CAGR: 25% over FY26–29.
- EV driveline, differential gears and traction motors.
- Strong electrification play.
- Growth driven by rising EV content.

**ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems**
- EPS CAGR: 29%.
- Market leader in braking systems.
- Strong exposure to ACE commercial vehicles.
- ACE: Autonomous, Connected & Electric.
- FY28E P/E: ~40x.

**Sansera Engineering**
- EPS CAGR: 33%.
- Precision-forged and machined components.
- Growing EV exposure.
- Expanding into aerospace and non-auto segments.
- FY28E P/E: ~44x.

**SJS Enterprises**
- EPS CAGR: 28%.
- Differentiated design-to-delivery aesthetics player.
- Supplies automotive and consumer companies.
- FY28E P/E: ~30x.
- Offers relatively better growth-valuation balance.

**Dhoot Transmission**
- EPS CAGR: 23%.
- Leading 2W/3W wiring-harness player.
- Strong EV exposure.
- Rising electronics content provides growth opportunity.
- FY28E P/E: ~35x.

**Uno Minda**
- EPS CAGR: 22%.
- Diversified across switches and lighting.
- Exposure to acoustics, alloy wheels and sensors.
- EV components add further growth.
- Strong content-per-vehicle opportunity.
- FY28E P/E: ~41x.

**Tube Investments of India**
- EPS CAGR: 42%.
- Highest projected EPS growth among the listed names.
- Precision tubes and auto components remain core businesses.
- Newer mobility businesses add growth optionality.
- FY28E P/E: ~49x.
- EV/EBITDA: ~16x.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Auto ancillaries could deliver ~23% EPS CAGR over FY26–29.
- Growth is available across multiple companies.
- Valuation is the key differentiator.
- SJS, Dhoot and Sansera offer a balance of growth and business quality.
- Sona, ZF, Uno Minda and TII require strong execution to justify premium valuations.
- Long-term winners should increase content per vehicle.
- Market-share gains and moving up the value chain remain key.
